## Questions to Evaluate Business Marketing Software


### What Marketing Goals Should the Software Help Me Achieve?


Before comparing marketing software for small business, take a step back and identify what you need it to do.


Maybe you want more people to find your business online. Perhaps you need a better way to keep your website and business listings updated, create social media content, or encourage customers to leave reviews. Your goals will help you determine which features are worth testing.

Start by asking yourself:


- Do I need to improve my online visibility?


- Do I want to attract more website visitors or customer inquiries?


- Am I spending too much time creating and publishing content?


- Do I need a more consistent way to manage my online reputation?


- Which marketing tasks are falling behind because I don’t have enough time?


Write down your top two or three priorities before starting the trial. That way, you can evaluate the software against your actual needs instead of getting distracted by features you may never use.


### Which Features Are Included in the Free Trial?


Not every business software free trial gives you access to every feature. Some platforms limit functionality, while others provide access to selected tools or plans for a set period.


Before signing up, find out exactly what you can test.


Depending on your marketing goals, useful features may include:

- **Social media marketing:**[Plan, create, and publish content](https://www.thryv.com/features/ai-for-small-businesses/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial#ai-content-assistant) to stay connected with your audience.


- **Online listings management:** Keep important[business information consistent](https://www.thryv.com/features/local-listings/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) across online directories.


- **Review management:** Monitor customer feedback and make it easier to[request and respond to reviews](https://www.thryv.com/features/ai-for-small-businesses/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial#ai-review-response) .


- **AI-powered marketing tools:**[Get help generating content](https://www.thryv.com/features/ai-for-small-businesses/) , improving efficiency, or managing repetitive tasks.


- **Marketing performance insights:** Understand how your[marketing efforts are performing](https://www.thryv.com/features/growth-package/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) .


Look for a trial that lets you experience the features most relevant to your business. If a platform advertises an impressive set of tools but restricts the ones you need, you may not get a fair picture of its value.

### Can I Manage Multiple Marketing Tasks in One Place?


Small business owners often juggle several marketing activities at once. You might update your website in one tool, schedule social posts in another, and manage customer reviews somewhere else.


Using separate tools isn’t necessarily a problem, but switching between platforms can make marketing harder to keep up with.


During your free trial, consider whether the software helps bring related marketing activities together. Look at how easily you can move between tasks and whether the platform reduces the number of steps required to get things done.


Ask yourself:


- Can I manage the marketing activities I use most often in one place?


- Will I need additional subscriptions to access essential features?


- Does the platform fit the way I currently work?


- Could consolidating tools reduce duplicate work or unnecessary expenses?


A[growth marketing platform](https://www.thryv.com/blog/ai-powered-growth-platform/) may simplify your routine, especially if you’re managing marketing yourself or working with a small team. The goal isn’t to have the most tools. It’s to have the right tools working together.


### How Can Automation and AI Simplify My Marketing?


Marketing consistently takes time. You need to create content, maintain your online presence, respond to reviews, and keep up with customer expectations.


Automation and AI-powered features can[help reduce some of that work](https://www.thryv.com/blog/ai-powered-platform-services/) . However, the value depends on how well those features support your actual workflow.


During the trial, look for opportunities to simplify repetitive tasks. Depending on the platform, that could mean using AI to help draft marketing content, streamline review responses, or speed up routine marketing activities.


Try asking:


- Can AI help me get started when I’m short on content ideas?


- Can I automate repetitive tasks without losing control over the final result?


- Can I review and customize AI-generated content before publishing?


- Will these features save meaningful time each week?


You don’t need to be an AI expert to benefit from AI-powered marketing software. Look for tools that are straightforward to use and give you practical help without adding another complicated process to your day.


### Is the Software Easy to Learn and Use?


A platform can have all the features you need and still be the wrong fit if it’s too complicated to use consistently.


This is particularly important for small business owners who don’t have a dedicated marketing team. You need tools that help you get work done, not software that requires hours of training before you can begin.


As you test the platform, pay attention to the setup process and your everyday experience.


Consider:


- How long does it take to get started?


- Are the main features easy to find?


- Can I complete common tasks without searching for instructions?


- Are tutorials, help articles, or customer support available?


- Can another team member learn the platform without extensive training?


Don’t spend your entire trial exploring every menu. Start with a few real marketing tasks, such as drafting a social post or reviewing your business information online. If the platform makes those tasks easier, that’s a useful sign.

### Can I Improve My Online Visibility With the Platform?


Customers need to find your business before they can choose your services. That’s why online visibility should be part of your marketing software evaluation.


Depending on your business, customers may discover you through search engines, maps, online directories, social media, or recommendations from other customers.


During the trial, check whether the software supports the channels that matter most to your audience.


For example, you might evaluate whether it helps you:


- Maintain accurate business listings and contact information.


- Keep your website current and useful to potential customers.


- Publish social content that keeps your business visible.


- Monitor and respond to customer reviews.


- Support your search engine optimization (SEO) efforts.


If local customers are important to your business, pay particular attention to tools that help keep your business information accurate and your online presence consistent.


Remember that marketing software can’t guarantee better rankings, more leads, or a specific number of new customers. The trial should help you determine whether the platform gives you practical tools to improve your marketing efforts over time.


### How Will I Track Marketing Performance?


Marketing software should help you understand more than what you’ve published. It should also help you evaluate whether your efforts are moving you toward your goals.


Before the trial begins, identify a few measurements that matter to your business. Depending on the features available, you might look at website traffic, search visibility, social engagement, customer inquiries, review activity, or conversions.


Then ask:


- Which performance metrics can I access?


- Can I see the results of my marketing activities over time?


- Are the reports easy to understand?


- Can I connect the available insights to my marketing goals?


You may not have enough time during a short trial to measure long-term improvements. That’s OK. Focus on learning what the platform tracks, how clearly it presents information, and whether those insights can help you make better marketing decisions.


### What Will the Software Cost After the Trial?


A free trial gives you a chance to explore a platform, but you should understand the full cost before signing up.


Some small business marketing tools offer different subscription tiers, optional add-ons, or separate pricing for services. The lowest advertised price may not include every feature you need.


Before starting the trial, review:


- The regular subscription price after the trial.


- Which features are included in each plan.


- Whether add-ons or extra services cost more.


- Whether you need to enter payment information to sign up.


- When billing begins and how cancellation works.


Compare the cost with the time and resources the software could help you save. For example, a platform that combines several marketing activities might be worth considering if it replaces tools you already pay for.


However, don’t assume that a higher-priced platform will automatically deliver better results. Choose software that fits your budget and provides value for the marketing tasks you need to accomplish.

### What Happens When the Free Trial Ends?


Before you invest time setting up a new platform, understand what happens when the trial period is over.


A 30-day free trial can provide a useful window to explore features, test workflows, and decide whether the software suits your business. But the amount of time you need depends on the complexity of the platform and how often you use it.


Check whether your trial ends automatically, converts to a paid subscription, or requires you to select a plan. Find out whether your settings, content, or other work will remain available if you decide not to subscribe.


To make your decision easier, keep a simple record during the trial:


- **What worked:** Which features were useful and easy to use?


- **What saved time:** Which tasks became simpler or faster?


- **What’s missing:** Did you encounter limitations or need other tools?


- **What’s the value:** Does the platform justify the cost based on your needs?


At the end of the trial, compare your experience with the goals you set at the beginning. If the platform makes important marketing tasks easier and fits your budget, it may be a strong candidate. If it doesn’t address your priorities, keep evaluating your options.
